raw_response:
I farm only 10.1 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What I do is mostly what has worked on my land and what I see nearby. For wheat, I will still plant on time in early October after the summer field is cleared, use an improved local variety, put most of the fertilizer down as base, then see the color of the crop after winter and topdress once at jointing. Wheat cannot miss water here, so with the well I will give it about three irrigations if rainfall is normal. I will not chase very high yield, because fertilizer, water, and hired help all cost money, and some people in my family work off-farm, so labor must be kept simple.

For maize, the main thing is speed after wheat harvest. The window is short, so I will do light rotary tillage or direct seeding if I can hire the machine in time, then plant right away in mid-June. I will use hybrid seed because local people all use it and the stand is better. For fertilizer, I will not cut too much because maize responds well on my land, but I also will not spend like the big farms. I will put one base dressing and one topdressing around the big flare stage, and irrigate once or twice depending on rain. If weeds come early, I will spray herbicide; if insects are obvious, then I add insecticide. This way is steady, not fancy, but it suits my small farm and my cash.
